title: Best Features - the closing statement
story: The demonstration ends here and the team returns to the closing slides. This is not a screen walkthrough. It names the features the team considers strongest and, for each one, the reason it is more than record keeping. Every feature named has already been demonstrated, so each point refers the panel back to a case they have watched and, if asked, the screen can be opened again with the account named in that case.

The features are presented after the demonstration rather than before it. The presentation that opened the session was a problem statement; the features only mean something once the panel has seen them run.
accounts: If a screen is requested again
the account named in the case referred to
Sign in by typing, as in {case:signin}; a student whose case was used up is put back with {case:reset-demo}
data: Rules with a source on every screen: {case:business-rules}, and the rules panels inside {case:withdrawal}, {case:enrollment}, {case:dropping} and {case:leave-of-absence}
A policy library and an assistant that cites its source, asked live: {case:policy-documents}, {case:policy-assistant}
Panel matching that differs per paper and shows why: {case:panel_matching}
Defense scheduling with hard and soft conflict warnings, and calendars for every role: {case:defense-scheduling}, {case:calendars}
Shared staged boards and reports computed from the records: {case:leave-of-absence}, {case:practicum}, {case:graduation}, {case:reports}

parts.title: Part A - Name the five features
parts.intro: These are statements for the presenters to say, one per feature. Each ends with the case to point back to.
steps: **Rules with a source.** Every rule the workflows follow sits in one register, with the Handbook or Protocol page it comes from and a label saying whether the system enforces it (Enforced by the system), only documents it (Documented only) or still needs review (Needs review, for the rules that are prototype assumptions). The same rules appear on the workflow screen where they apply, under Rules applied on this screen, and a refusal message quotes the rule. This answers the panel's question about dropping a subject on Day 1 ({case:business-rules}, {case:withdrawal}, {case:dropping}).

**A policy library and a cited answer.** Staff add policy documents, keep version history and mark one as Draft until the Graduate School validates it. The Policy Assistant answers from those documents and names the document and the page it used, for staff, Dean, faculty and students; when the library does not cover a question it says so instead of guessing, and each answer is labelled with how it was made (Offline answer for a keyword match, Answered by Gemini when a key is set) ({case:policy-documents}, {case:policy-assistant}).

**Panel matching that explains itself.** The shortlist is scored out of 100 from the similarity between the paper and each faculty member's expertise records (60 points), their availability (25) and their workload (15), and the breakdown is on screen. Different papers produce different rankings, the student's own adviser is never offered, and a person chooses the panel ({case:panel_matching}).

**Scheduling that checks before it books.** The system reads availability, shows the best shared options, warns of conflicts and says whether a warning is a hard stop (a double-booked panelist or room, a declined invitation, a slot in the past) or a soft one that can be overridden with a recorded reason. Panelists answer invitations, and the booked defense appears in the calendar of staff, Dean, faculty and student; a faculty member may also connect Google Calendar ({case:defense-scheduling}, {case:calendars}).

**Shared boards and reports computed from records.** Leave of Absence, Readmission, Practicum and Graduation run on the same staged boards, with the same Board and Table views, where a card is moved from stage to stage by drag and drop or by Move to... and every move is recorded. Reports & Analytics is computed from those records, not typed in: five filterable reports, the Registrar's daily list, and charts whose figures open the students behind them ({case:leave-of-absence}, {case:practicum}, {case:graduation}, {case:reports}).

parts.title: Part B - State the common thread and close
steps: Say plainly what connects the five: each one takes data the Graduate School already holds, together with the policy that governs it, and produces a decision, a warning or a measurement from it, instead of only storing and retrieving a record.
Invite the panel to return to any screen already demonstrated if they want a feature shown again.

Close with the declared limits in Section 9, Honest Notes & Limitations: no email is sent from the portal, Google Calendar is optional and per faculty member, official student, enrollment and grade data come only from the AIMS import and cannot be edited here, the Operations Manual is a Draft until the Graduate School validates it, and rules marked Needs review are prototype values.

notes: Features are named after the demonstration, on the closing slides, because each of them refers to something the panel has already watched run.
The case slugs used in the references were the ones in the cases folder on 2026-11-02; the references must follow any later rename.
